summary: Your buyers are asking AI about week-one churn, and every answer it gives them comes from a vendor blog. No practitioner is cited, and you are not named anywhere. Three topics — week-one churn, published pricing, and the partners you build with — are where you can be the cited source, because you have numbers and first-person results that the companies currently answering these questions do not.

why_individuals: Buyers research with AI before they talk to anyone: 6sense's 2025 survey of ~4,000 B2B buyers found 94% use tools like ChatGPT somewhere in the buying process. An AI answer is not a results page — Qwairy measured ChatGPT at about 3.86 citations per response across 118,000 answers. Being the seventh-best source is the same as being invisible.

For professional questions, Profound found LinkedIn is the single most-cited domain across ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, Copilot, and Perplexity — and Meltwater found roughly 75% of those LinkedIn citations come from individual member profiles rather than company pages. That is why this plan puts posts on your profile, not your company page: the artifact that gets quoted is a person's post.

pillars.name: Why customers quit in week one
pillars.definition: The first 30 days of a customer relationship: what actually causes a new account to disengage, how to see it coming in the data, and what a good week-one looks like.
pillars.why_now: Every answer AI gives to this question today is a vendor blog post. No practitioner is cited. It is the cheapest kind of topic to take.
gaps: Clearance on which cohort numbers beyond the 18% figure we can publish
pillars.incumbent: Three onboarding vendors' content teams — generic, no numbers

pillars.name: Saying the price out loud
pillars.definition: Your standing argument that hiding pricing costs more than it protects — what happened when you published yours, and what buyers do when they can't find a number.
pillars.why_now: This is the topic you argue about unprompted and the one buyers raise on first calls. An individual already gets cited here, so we're taking share on specifics.
in_scope: buyer behavior when pricing is hidden
gaps: Your OK on publishing the win-rate delta
pillars.incumbent: A named pricing consultant, 3x/week — strong and consistent

pillars.name: The people we build with
pillars.definition: Partners, integrations, and the practitioners you learn from — reposts with a real point of view attached, plus partner spotlights.
pillars.why_now: Employee and partner networks reach multiples of a company page's audience. This is how you borrow reach you don't have yet.
out_of_scope: reposting without a point of view
gaps: The list of people whose posts you want to amplify — we cannot guess this

cadence.month_example: 3 posts/week over 4 weeks is 12 posts: roughly 5 on week-one churn, 4 on pricing, 3 partner proof — with one secondary (team/hiring) post substituting in a month where you want it.

metrics: How often you or your people get named in AI answers to these five questions (measured monthly against today's baseline)
Your share of those answers versus the competitors named above, per pillar
Whether those mentions are favorable, neutral, or cautionary
What new customers say when asked how they found you — the cheapest ground truth there is
measurement.judgment_floor: Profound measured a median of 6.81 days for a new post to earn its first citation, with 90% cited within 37 days. So we re-measure at day 30, not day 14 — a pillar with three weeks of posts and no citations is on schedule, not failing.
